system.name: S2Sim
system.one_liner: a selective symbolic-simulation tool that diagnoses and repairs distributed routing configuration errors by checking them against intent-compliant contracts

content.subject: one symbolic-simulation run computing each router's route and flagging two contract violations (c1, c2) on an example network

content.key_idea: Running the symbolic simulation on the example network surfaces exactly two contract violations, c1 at C and c2 at F, and shows how forcing them changes which route each router finally selects.

summary: This figure from S2Sim's appendix illustrates Step 2 of the paper's symbolic simulation on a six-router example network (A-F) that originates a prefix p at D. Each router lists its candidate routes (r0-r11); the route it finally selects is underlined. Where the original configuration would violate an intent-compliant contract, the affected route and its forcing condition are coloured red: C's decision to not export [C,D] to B violates contract c1, so the simulation forces it, and B then selects r3 [B,C,D]. Downstream, F would prefer the longer [F,A,B,C,D] path, violating contract c2 together with c1, so the simulation forces F to keep r7 [F,E,D] instead. A table beneath the graph spells out both violated contracts, c1 and c2, in full.
summary_zh: 该图展示S2Sim对示例网络的符号模拟：各路由器列出候选路由r0-r11，下划线标最终选择；C违反合约c1被强制后B选r3；F因c1∧c2被迫保留r7而非更长路径，下方表格给出c1、c2定义。
